extracted.intended_audience: aspiring cozy-mystery writers and fans/readers interested in the genre
extracted.subtask_description: A concise genre guide describing the conventions, tone, character types, settings, and thematic niches that define cozy mysteries, useful for writers and readers who want to understand or produce cozy whodunnits.

rubrics_metrics.name: No graphic violence / no explicit sex or swearing
rubrics_metrics.description: There’s no strict definition for the cozy mystery, though the main rule of thumb seems to be that the story contains no graphic violence and generally, no swearing or sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep descriptions of the crime and its aftermath non-gratuitous and avoid explicit sexual content and profanity; the genre trades on comfort and readability rather than shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lighthearted tone and escapism
rubrics_metrics.description: These are more lighthearted crime narratives—you won’t be so disturbed that you need to sleep with lights on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for an overall reassuring, comforting tone that provides escapism rather than bleakness; balance suspense with warmth and wit so readers remain entertained, not traumatized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on plot and character development
rubrics_metrics.description: A focus on plot and character development ensures a predictable and reassuring experience offering escapism without being too heavy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize a well-constructed mystery plot (clues, red herrings, resolution) alongside rounded characters whose relationships and personalities drive both interest and the solving of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amateur sleuth protagonist who uses intellect and life experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Importantly, the cozy mystery’s protagonist is an amateur sleuth who uses intellect and life experience to solve a case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a protagonist whose non-professional perspective, practical knowledge, or hobby-related expertise plausibly leads them to investigate and solve the crime (e.g., Miss Marple-style observational deduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional investment and community knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: These affable amateur detectives typically have an emotional investment behind their probing. They also know their neighbor’s quirks and habits, elicit confidences, and ultimately work out the solution before law enforcement does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the sleuth personal stakes or motives for investigating and exploit their embeddedness in a community—intimate local knowledge and relationships supply clues and access other investigators lack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor and idiosyncratic secondary characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides a crime-solving amateur sleuth, cozy mysteries enjoy other appealing conventions. The stories have humor, idiosyncratic secondary characters...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate the world with colorful, quirky supporting characters who add warmth and comic relief; use character quirks as both entertainment and possible clue/obstruction devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close-knit communities and quaint/charming setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy mysteries enjoy... closeknit communities where everyone knows each other. ...there’s often a quaint or charming element—an animal sidekick, for example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set the story in a small town, village, or tight social microcosm (or a cozy milieu like a bookshop, bakery, knitting circle) where social intimacy heightens both motive and opportunity and creates a comforting atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victim is generally unlikeable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider making the victim morally ambiguous or unpleasant to reduce reader distress, create understandable motives among suspects, and simplify moral alignment in the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension with police / sleuth viewed as meddlesome
rubrics_metrics.description: While the amateur detective may have some 'in' on the police force, officers find them meddlesome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray professional investigators as competent but wary of the amateur; the sleuth’s relationship with law enforcement can generate conflict, obstacles, or occasional cooperation that propels the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast pacing with twists and red herrings
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozies are usually fast-paced and involve at least one unexpected turn of events and red herrings to distract us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep momentum through brisk chaptering and scene pacing; plant plausible red herrings and at least one significant twist to surprise readers while still playing fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution restores order
rubrics_metrics.description: And we can count on things being put right again by story’s end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End with a clear resolution that solves the crime, restores community equilibrium, and delivers emotional closure—readers expect comfort and a return to normalcy after the mystery is solved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden Age / whodunnit puzzle conventions and fair-play clueing
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozies harken back to... the Golden Age of Detective Fiction... Their work playfully misleads readers while simultaneously encouraging them to solve the crime alongside the protagonist. Remote settings like an English country house or an abandoned island were featured, as well as a short-list of suspects from distinctive upper-class professions, and bodies discovered in unlikely places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt puzzle-like plotting: present all essential clues openly, use a limited suspect pool and closed settings when appropriate, and mislead playfully rather than deceptively so readers can engage in solving the mystery (Agatha Christie/Miss Marple as models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible sub-themes and niche hooks
rubrics_metrics.description: The cozy sub-category of crime stories runs wide and deep, from historical cozy mysteries to romance and paranormal cozies. Cozy book series feature professions ranging from beauticians and bookstore owners to teachers; share themes like pets, cooking, and holidays; and showcase hobbies such as genealogy, knitting, and travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a strong niche or recurring hook (profession, hobby, holiday, pet theme, historical period, paranormal element, etc.) to differentiate a series and attract a target audience; cozies lend themselves to serial protagonists and themed installments.
